plain_6parts.title: Part 1 of 6 — Background and global conventions
plain_6parts.text:
Implement a reconciliation tool for an e-commerce settlement team. These rules apply throughout the tool:

- Store every amount as integer cents and process only `USD` records.
- Silently skip invalid records; never raise or print for bad input.
- An amount whose absolute value exceeds `1,000,000` cents (`$10,000.00`) is invalid.
- A timestamp may use either `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, with valid calendar values. Other formats are invalid.
- Trim both identifiers. Every `ORDER_ID` must start with the exact prefix `ORD-`.

plain_6parts.title: Part 2 of 6 — Data and release-wide rules
plain_6parts.text:
Each line has six `|`-separated fields:

```text
TYPE|RECORD_ID|ORDER_ID|AMOUNT|CURRENCY|TIMESTAMP
```

`TYPE` is case-insensitive `ORDER` or `PAYMENT` and is stored uppercase. IDs must remain non-empty after trimming. Amounts contain digits and at most one decimal point, with an optional leading minus sign. Scientific notation is invalid. At most three fractional digits are accepted; round a third digit to cents using round-half-up. Negative orders are invalid and negative payments are refunds. Duplicate record IDs keep the first valid occurrence.

Only refunds whose `order_id` belongs to an existing order count toward the refund total. Final unmatched order IDs must be unique. Final `net_total` cannot be negative and is reported as `0` when the calculation is below zero. The final summary includes a key named exactly `refund_total`.

plain_6parts.title: Part 3 of 6 — Summary report
plain_6parts.text: `build_summary(matches, refund_total)` returns exactly five keys: `total_orders`, `matched_count`, `refund_total`, `net_total`, and `unmatched_ids`. Count results whose status is exactly lowercase `matched`. `net_total` is matched payment amounts minus `refund_total`, with the zero lower bound stated earlier. `unmatched_ids` is a deduplicated ascending lexicographic list.

plain_6parts.title: Part 4 of 6 — Payment matching
plain_6parts.text: `match_payments(records)` returns one result per order in retained order-record order. A non-refund payment initially qualifies from the order timestamp through exactly 72 hours later, subject to the release clarification in Part 6. If several qualify, choose the earliest timestamp and break an exact tie by retained source order. Refunds never match. Each result has exactly `order_id`, `status`, and `amount`; status is lowercase `matched` or `unmatched`, and unmatched amount is `0`.

plain_6parts.title: Part 5 of 6 — Parsing, loading, and refunds
plain_6parts.text:
`parse_amount(s)` applies all amount syntax, rounding, and limit rules; negative values remain negative because payment refunds need them. Apply the `1,000,000` limit after conversion to cents. `parse_record(line)` applies the six-field format, ID, currency, timestamp, and negative-order rules and returns a dictionary with exactly `type`, `record_id`, `order_id`, `amount`, `currency`, and `timestamp`, or `None`. `load_records(text)` silently skips invalid rows, preserves input order, and keeps the first valid duplicate record ID. `compute_refunds(records)` returns the positive sum of qualifying negative payment amounts under the existing-order rule.

Functions do not mutate input objects or store global state.

plain_6parts.title: Part 6 of 6 — Release clarification
plain_6parts.text: The released matching window changes the endpoint stated in Part 4: a payment must occur **strictly less than 72 hours** after the order. A payment at exactly 72 hours is outside the window. The order timestamp itself remains included. No other rule changes.

reference_steps.title: Step 1 of 6 — Implement parse_amount(s)
reference_steps.text: Convert an amount string to integer cents. Allow digits, one decimal point, and optional leading minus; negative values remain negative for refunds. Reject scientific notation. Accept at most three fractional digits and round the third half-up: 0.005 becomes 1 and -0.005 becomes -1. After conversion, reject abs(cents) over 1,000,000. Return None silently.

reference_steps.title: Step 2 of 6 — Implement parse_record(line)
reference_steps.text: Parse TYPE|RECORD_ID|ORDER_ID|AMOUNT|CURRENCY|TIMESTAMP. Type is case-insensitive ORDER or PAYMENT and stored uppercase. Trim non-empty IDs; every order ID starts with exact prefix ORD-. Use parse_amount; negative orders are invalid and negative payments are valid refunds. Currency must be USD. Accept exactly YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS by attempting the minute format and then the seconds format. Return exactly type, record_id, order_id, amount, currency, timestamp, or None silently.

reference_steps.title: Step 3 of 6 — Implement load_records(text)
reference_steps.text: Parse each line, silently skip invalid rows, and preserve input order. Duplicate trimmed record IDs keep the first valid occurrence; an invalid occurrence does not reserve the ID. Empty or non-string input returns an empty list.

reference_steps.title: Step 4 of 6 — Implement compute_refunds(records)
reference_steps.text: A refund is a negative PAYMENT. Count it only when its order_id belongs to an existing ORDER. Return the positive sum or 0. Do not mutate records.

reference_steps.title: Step 5 of 6 — Implement match_payments(records)
reference_steps.text: Return one result per order. A non-negative payment qualifies when order_id matches and its time is at or after the order but strictly less than 72 hours later; exactly 72 hours is outside the released window. Choose the earliest, retaining source order for ties. Refunds never match. Return exactly order_id, status, amount, using lowercase matched or unmatched and unmatched amount 0.

reference_steps.title: Step 6 of 6 — Implement build_summary(matches, refund_total)
reference_steps.text: Return exactly total_orders, matched_count, refund_total, net_total, and unmatched_ids. Count lowercase matched results. net_total is matched amounts minus refund_total but cannot be negative. Deduplicate unmatched order IDs and sort them lexicographically.
